riscos.descricao: Técnicas de raciocínio por processo podem aumentar tempo de inferência e consumo de tokens; o conteúdo intermediário aumenta a geração de tokens e o custo computacional. O estudo mede só tokens médios do conteúdo intermediário como proxy (Figura 5); custo monetário e tempo não quantificados.
Mesmo com decodificação gulosa, pequenas variações podem ocorrer por erros de precisão de ponto flutuante e ambientes de execução não determinísticos.

Técnicas de prompting podem reduzir a correção em relação ao Direct prompting: few-shot ficou abaixo do Direct prompting no HumanEval com LLaMA3-8B-Instruct, e em problemas difíceis do LiveCodeBench a maioria das linhas de base ficou abaixo do Direct prompting (GPT-3.5-Turbo).
A geração de objetivos em zero-shot pode variar em formato, detalhe ou clareza entre instâncias; a qualidade dos objetivos gerados não foi avaliada (limitação declarada).

citacoes.trecho: This paper introduces Chain of Grounded Objectives (CGO), a concise goal-oriented prompting approach that embeds functional objectives into prompts to enhance code generation.
CGO first prompts the LLM to analyze the given problem and autonomously generate a compact set of objectives outlining the functional requirements of the solution.
These objectives are then incorporated as supplemental input to guide the final code generation step.
Direct prompting: Generates code solely from the problem description.
Few-shot: Includes example problems and solutions to guide the model.
CodeCoT: Utilizes Chain of Thought (CoT) with a one-shot example to generate intermediate steps and final code in two stages [11].
Zero-shot CoT: A prompt that generates a CoT Reasoning process to solve the given problem without providing example CoT and incorporates it into code generation [17].
Self-Planning: Extracts sub-tasks from the problem and generates a plan, which guides code generation in two stages [16].
Subsequently, use the generated pseudocode to write the final code in three stage.
For the implementation of Chain-of-Thought (CoT) [23, 32] and Self-Planning strategies, reasoning chains were constructed based on code examples provided in the original Self-Planning approach.
Few-shot prompting was realized by randomly selecting example problems and their corresponding solutions from the same dataset.
To evaluate whether minor wording differences could significantly influence the effectiveness of the CGO approach, we conducted an experiment.

Based on our preliminary experiments, while effective, process-oriented reasoning can introduce unnecessary complexity in straightforward tasks, potentially leading to increased inference time and token consumption.
While this additional content helps guide the code generation process, it also increases token generation, thereby raising the computational cost of using LLMs.

Although greedy sampling typically produces the same output for a given prompt, minor variations may still occur due to factors such as floating-point precision errors and non-deterministic execution environments.
To account for this, we repeated the experiment 10 times per problem.
While it showed improvements in MBPP-sanitized and MBPP+, it underperformed compared to direct prompting on the HumanEval benchmarks.
Performance degradation was more apparent in hard problems, where most baselines underperformed compared to DP.
CGO generates objectives using a zero-shot approach, which may lead to variations in format, detail, or clarity across different instances.
To increase the diversity of outputs, we generated n = 10 objective samples per problem, which were subsequently used to guide the code generation process.
